properties.natural_language: Block numbers in GetBlockBodies and GetReceipts requests must be validated against the Paris upgrade boundary (block 15,537,393) before serving data.
Requests for block data targeting blocks before block 15,537,393 must be rejected by eth/70 nodes.
After a valid post-PoS data request is processed, the requested block bodies and receipts must be returned to the requesting peer.
After protocol upgrade completes, the client must refuse to serve pre-PoS block data via the eth/70 protocol.
The Paris upgrade boundary block number (15,537,393) must be an immutable constant used consistently across all message scope validation.
All four affected message types (GetBlockBodies 0x05, BlockBodies 0x06, GetReceipts 0x0f, Receipts 0x10) must pass scope validation before processing.
During the mixed-protocol transition period, eth/69 and eth/70 clients must coexist on the network without consensus failure.
Pre-PoS historical data must remain accessible through alternative mechanisms (archive nodes, Era files) when eth/70 stops serving it.
Light clients must be able to securely trust post-PoS data without requiring pre-PoS historical verification.
Genesis configuration data fetched from yolonet.xyz must be integrity-checked before initializing node state. HTTPS must be enforced for the fetch.
Genesis JSON data must be a valid JSON document conforming to the expected genesis configuration schema before loading.
Peer list data received from the EF bootnode must be validated for well-formed enode URLs before connecting to listed peers.
Bootnode connection must be authenticated via the enode public key to prevent MITM attacks on peer discovery.
Node operator configuration parameters must be validated before use to prevent misconfiguration attacks.
Contract bytecode submitted by developers must undergo full EVM sandbox validation and gas limit enforcement before deployment on the testnet.
After genesis configuration is loaded, the node must have initialized with the correct network ID and chain parameters.
After successful bootnode connection, the node must be able to discover additional peers on the Yolo testnet.
After contract deployment, execution of experimental opcodes (EIP-2315 subroutines, EIP-2537 BLS precompiles) must produce correct results.
The testnet must be treated as ephemeral with no persistence guarantees; it can be destroyed at any time without notice.
No production applications or real value must be deployed on the ephemeral testnet.
After block 2,463,000, all IO-heavy operations (SLOAD, BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, CALL, etc.) must use the repriced EIP-150 gas costs.
The block number must be checked against the fork activation block (2,463,000) before selecting which gas cost schedule to apply.
Gas costs for IO operations must always reflect their true computational resource cost to prevent underpricing-based DoS attacks.
All network participants must be running fork-compatible client versions at or before block 2,463,000 to prevent chain splits.
After the fork deploys, the same DoS attack using IO-heavy operations must become economically infeasible due to increased gas costs.
After gas deduction, if remaining gas is insufficient for an IO operation, the execution must halt with an out-of-gas error.
Block header received from a network peer must contain a valid difficulty value that matches the expected difficulty computed using EIP-649 rules.
Block and uncle headers from miners must pass full consensus validation including difficulty, timestamp, and transaction validity checks.
After computing the fake block number (max(0, block_number - 3,000,000)), the difficulty bomb component must use this delayed value instead of the actual block number.
After Byzantium fork activation, the block reward must be exactly 3 ETH (3e18 wei), not the pre-fork 5 ETH.
Uncle rewards must be calculated as (8-k) * 3 ETH / 8 where k is the uncle age, and nephew reward must be 3 ETH / 32.
After difficulty comparison, if claimed difficulty does not match expected difficulty, the block must be rejected.
The BYZANTIUM_FORK_BLKNUM must be consistently configured across all clients (4,370,000 for mainnet) to prevent chain splits.
The reduced block reward (3 ETH) must maintain sufficient mining incentive to prevent hash rate drops that could enable 51% attacks.
The wallet browser extension must inject the EthereumProvider object before any DApp can use it for blockchain interactions.
RequestArguments must contain a valid 'method' string field before being passed to Provider.request().
Sensitive methods (signing, account access) must require user authorization before execution.
After receiving a JSON-RPC response, the provider must translate it to native JavaScript objects before resolving the promise.
When an error occurs, the provider must reject the promise with a ProviderRpcError containing a valid error code (4001, 4100, 4200, 4900, or 4901) and descriptive message.
Error code 4001 must only be returned when the user explicitly rejected the request via the wallet UI.
The JavaScript runtime must provide adequate isolation between DApp code and provider internals to prevent unauthorized access.
Provider request must always return a Promise that either resolves with a result or rejects with a ProviderRpcError; it must never hang indefinitely.
Error 4900 (Disconnected) and 4901 (Chain Disconnected) must be semantically distinct: 4900 indicates complete provider failure while 4901 indicates specific chain unavailability.
Before executing any bitwise operation, the EVM stack must contain at least the required number of operands (2 for AND/OR/XOR, 1 for NOT).
Before executing a BYTE extraction, the byte index must be checked against the 256-bit word boundary (index < 32).
Before executing a shift operation, the shift amount must be checked against 256 to determine if overflow handling applies.
All bitwise operations must have at least GAS_VERY_LOW (3 gas) available before execution.
After a BYTE extraction with index >= 32, the result pushed to stack must be exactly 0.
After SHL with shift >= 256, the result must be 0. After SHR with shift >= 256, the result must be 0. After SAR with shift >= 256, the result must be 0 (positive input) or MAX_VALUE (negative input).
After SHL execution, the result must be masked to MAX_VALUE (2^256 - 1) to prevent values exceeding 256 bits.
After gas deduction for a bitwise operation, if gas was insufficient, execution must halt with an out-of-gas exception and no state changes.
All bitwise operations (AND, OR, XOR, NOT, BYTE, SHL, SHR, SAR) must cost exactly GAS_VERY_LOW (3 gas) uniformly.
All bitwise operations must be constant-time for same input sizes to prevent timing side-channel attacks.
The underlying 256-bit integer arithmetic must handle shift operations correctly without overflow or truncation errors.
Before DUP operations, the stack must have at least N elements (where N is the DUP position parameter) or execution must halt with StackUnderflowError.
Before SWAP operations, the stack must have at least N+1 elements (where N is the SWAP position parameter) or execution must halt with StackUnderflowError.
PUSH and DUP operations must not push values onto the stack if doing so would exceed the maximum stack depth of 1024 elements.
After a PUSH operation, the stack must have one additional element on top equal to the value read from bytecode, and the program counter must advance by 1 + N bytes.
After a POP operation, the top stack element must be removed and discarded, and the program counter must advance by 1.
After a DUP operation, the stack must have a copy of the element at position N on top, with all other elements unchanged.
After a SWAP operation, the top element and element at position N must be exchanged, with all other elements unchanged.
After a failed stack bounds check, execution must halt with StackUnderflowError and all state changes must be reverted.
PUSH0 must cost GAS_BASE (2 gas) while PUSH1-PUSH32 must cost GAS_VERY_LOW (3 gas).
Bytecode must be immutable during execution; PUSH operations reading immediate bytes from bytecode must not be affected by concurrent modifications.
The program counter must only be modifiable through explicit control flow operations (JUMP, JUMPI) or standard instruction advancement; it cannot be arbitrarily manipulated.
Stack access must be O(1) time complexity for any position to prevent performance-based denial-of-service attacks.
Transaction signatures must include a chain ID (per EIP-155) to prevent replay attacks from other chains after the Spurious Dragon fork.
Transactions from attackers attempting replay from other chains must have their chain ID checked and rejected if it does not match the network's chain ID.
After block 2,675,000, all four Spurious Dragon EIPs (155, 160, 161, 170) must be simultaneously active.
After state clearing (EIP-161), any account that is touched and found to be empty (nonce=0, balance=0, no code) must be removed from the state trie.
After EIP-170 activation, contract deployment must fail if the resulting bytecode exceeds 24KB (24,576 bytes).
All node operators must upgrade to Spurious Dragon compatible clients before block 2,675,000 to prevent chain splits.
The referenced execution-specs and consensus-specs repositories must contain correct and complete specifications for their respective upgrades.
The timestamp-based activation mechanism must synchronize EL and CL upgrades to prevent activation timing mismatches.
After specification consistency validation, if any discrepancy is detected between EL and CL spec references, it must be flagged as an inconsistency.
Block headers must pass all validation checks (sequential numbering, timestamp ordering, gas limit bounds, difficulty match, parent hash) before ommer validation proceeds.
Ommer blocks must satisfy: maximum 2 per block, no duplicates, age between 1-6 blocks, valid ancestry, and not already in the canonical chain.
Transaction validation must check: sufficient intrinsic gas, block gas available, valid ECDSA signature, nonce match, sufficient balance (gas*price + value), and sender is EOA.
After all transactions in a block are executed, the computed state root, transaction root, receipt root, and logs bloom must match the values claimed in the block header.
After transaction execution, the gas refund must be capped at 50% of gas consumed (Byzantium-specific rule).
After block finalization, the miner must receive exactly 3 ETH base reward plus (3 ETH / 32) per included ommer.
After PoW validation, the hashimoto result as uint must be <= (2^256) / difficulty or the block must be rejected.
Empty account cleanup must never delete accounts that have non-zero balance, non-zero nonce, or existing code.
The block gas limit must be within parent_gas_limit +/- (parent_gas_limit / 1024) and must be at least 5000.
The difficulty bomb calculation must use the delayed block number (block_number - 3,000,000) and only add the bomb component when the resulting exponent is positive.
